prerequisites: Good knowledge of Statistical Prediction Models

learning_outcomes.text: Apply advanced linear modeling methods to real data, statistically analyzing their effectiveness.
Understand what dynamic regression models consist of, being able to apply them to data where necessary.
Apply classification techniques to time series analysis.
Know advanced time series models and their connections with other data science techniques.
Critically analyze the different forecasting methods studied and apply the most appropriate in each case.
Apply advanced forecasting techniques to real data and generate associated reports.

syllabus_topics: Non-linear relationships. Regression splines. Local linear regression. Logistic regression.
Estimation in dynamic regression models. Regression with ARIMA errors. Forecasts. Stochastic and deterministic trends. Dynamic harmonic regression.
Hierarchical time series. Grouped time series. Bottom-up, top-down, and middle-out approaches. Optimal reconciliation.
Complex seasonality patterns. Autoregressive vectors. Machine learning methods with temporal data.
teaching_methods: Academic tutoring (in-person and online via virtual campus forum or email)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participation in seminars and tutorials (includes online)
Active participation in forums and virtual campus activities

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is the sum of weighted scores from four components: attendance/participation (5%), active forum/virtual campus participation (10%), practical exams (40%), and a final theoretical exam (45%). No minimum grade is required for individual components. For the extraordinary call in July, students will take a theoretical/practical written exam (4.5 points) and a computer-based practical exam (4 points); these scores are added to the grades obtained in the course's participation components (1 and 2). For the extraordinary call in January, students can pass with a single theoretical-practical final exam covering 100% of the grade. Differentiated evaluation involves a single exam covering theory, classroom practices, and lab practices. In all cases, a minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the course.
